coverage_rule: Coverage is recorded per vector and requirement only where an assertion is actually executed. covered: executed by a checker published with the corpus against the shipped file. partial: declared in the manifest and executed only by the emitter that produced it or by an external run, or the checker exercises part of the requirement. not covered: no executed assertion. The reverse view takes the best coverage any vector gives a requirement within the corpora it names. The rev8 cross-check is, in its own README's words, not a conformance verifier: it checks roots, census and condition identifiers, so it can give 'covered' only to root-construction rules and to the four rev8 discriminating vectors.

D01.pinned_by: examples/v0.3-composed/vectors.json spec + README; examples/v0.4-composed/vectors.json spec + README (both name -01)
D01.scope: whole document; every normative statement in sections 3-7, 9 and 10

requirements.D01-3.2-conjunction: §3.2: multiple verification.* constraints combine with AND; all MUST resolve to act for the action to proceed
requirements.D01-3.2-env-ordering: §3.2: environment.* constraints MUST short-circuit before verification.* constraints
requirements.D01-4.1-jws: §4.1: receipts MUST be JWS; a relying party MUST accept compact and JSON (flattened) serializations
requirements.D01-4.1-alg: §4.1: a conforming implementation MUST accept both EdDSA and ES256
requirements.D01-4.1-kid: §4.1: kid MUST resolve to a key in the issuer's published JWKS
requirements.D01-4.2-v_verdict: §4.2: v_verdict REQUIRED, one of supported | refuted | unverifiable | unknown
requirements.D01-4.2-v_adversarial_result: §4.2: v_adversarial_result REQUIRED, one of resilient | vulnerable | not_checked
requirements.D01-4.2-v_recommendation: §4.2: v_recommendation REQUIRED, derived deterministically from the canonical input under the named mapping
requirements.D01-4.2-v_gate: §4.2: v_gate REQUIRED, act | halt, derived from v_recommendation under the named mapping
requirements.D01-4.2-v_gate_mapping: §4.2: v_gate_mapping REQUIRED; mapping documents are immutable after publication
requirements.D01-4.2-v_gate_mapping_hash: §4.2: v_gate_mapping_hash REQUIRED; absence is a malformed-receipt condition and MUST halt
requirements.D01-4.2-jwt-claims: §4.2: iss, iat, exp REQUIRED; sub RECOMMENDED; nbf OPTIONAL
requirements.D01-4.3-sequence: §4.3: a relying party MUST execute the eight-step sequence and treat any failure as malformed with gate decision halt
requirements.D01-4.3-1-signature: §4.3 step 1: verify the JWS signature against the issuer's published JWKS
requirements.D01-4.3-2-mapping-digest: §4.3 step 2: fetch the named mapping document; its SHA-256 MUST match v_gate_mapping_hash; receipts without the hash are malformed
requirements.D01-4.3-3-recompute-recommendation: §4.3 step 3: recompute candidate_recommendation from (v_verdict, v_confidence, v_adversarial_result) using the mapping's rules and threshold
requirements.D01-4.3-7-time: §4.3 step 7: verify exp/nbf against current time subject to clock tolerance
requirements.D01-4.3-8-mismatch-halts: §4.3 step 8: any mismatch -> malformed; gate decision = halt
requirements.D01-4.4-v_claim: §4.4: the verified claim MUST be bound via v_claim (text, or hash REQUIRED when text is omitted)
requirements.D01-4.5-mapping-hash-present: §4.5: v_gate_mapping_hash MUST be present in all conforming receipts
requirements.D01-4.6-old-mapping-verifiable: §4.6: a receipt issued under an older mapping MUST remain verifiable as correct under that mapping
requirements.D01-4.6-mapping-immutable: §4.6: publishers MUST treat published mappings as immutable; new rules ship under new identifiers
requirements.D01-5.1-table-shape: §5.1: the binary act/halt shape derived from the canonical recommendation MUST be preserved
requirements.D01-5.1-row-1: §5.1 Table 2 row 1: supported, >= threshold, resilient -> confident_supported -> act
requirements.D01-5.1-row-2: §5.1 Table 2 row 2: supported, >= threshold, not_checked -> un_probed_not_cleared -> halt
requirements.D01-5.1-row-3: §5.1 Table 2 row 3: supported, any, vulnerable -> vulnerable_supported -> halt
requirements.D01-5.1-row-4: §5.1 Table 2 row 4: supported, < threshold, resilient or not_checked -> weak_supported -> halt
requirements.D01-5.1-row-6: §5.1 Table 2 row 6: unverifiable or unknown -> unverifiable -> halt
requirements.D01-5.1-row-7: §5.1 Table 2 row 7: error condition -> error -> halt
requirements.D01-5.2-threshold-from-mapping: §5.2: the threshold is recovered from the named mapping; two receipts under one mapping ID MUST gate against the same threshold
requirements.D01-5.2-uncertainty-halts: §5.2: un-probed adversarial state is not equivalent to resilient; uncertainty MUST halt (un_probed_not_cleared)
requirements.D01-5.2-no-foreign-threshold: §5.2: relying parties MUST NOT treat a receipt as conformant under a mapping with a different threshold than that mapping states
requirements.D01-5.3-fail-closed: §5.3: missing, malformed, expired, signature-invalid or unresolvable-mapping receipts MUST be treated as halt; implementations MUST NOT default to act
requirements.D01-6.2-stale-signature: §6.2: a stale signature makes the receipt invalid; relying party MUST treat as halt
requirements.D01-6.2-stale-calibration: §6.2: stale calibration SHOULD be re-evaluated; issuers SHOULD publish recalibration cadence
requirements.D01-6.2-stale-evidence: §6.2: stale evidence SHOULD be re-evaluated and MUST NOT be honored as a gate signal for new actions
requirements.D01-7.1-publish-anchors: §7.1: verifier issuers MUST publish calibration anchors (the listed items)
requirements.D01-7.1-harness: §7.1: verifier issuers SHOULD publish a reference reproduction harness under a permissive license
requirements.D01-7.2-cadence: §7.2: issuers SHOULD publish a recalibration cadence; v_calibration.valid_until SHOULD reflect it
requirements.D01-7.2-surface-stale: §7.2: relying parties consuming receipts with stale calibration SHOULD log and surface the staleness rather than silently accept
requirements.D01-9.1-ordering-holds: §9.1: the §3.2 ordering MUST hold when composed with environment.*
requirements.D01-9.2-key-rotation: §9.2: issuers MUST rotate JWKS keys on a published cadence; RPs MUST honor key revocation lists where published
requirements.D01-9.2-replay: §9.2: RPs MUST verify iat and exp against current time
requirements.D01-9.2-sample-harness: §9.2 (confidence inflation): RPs SHOULD periodically sample receipts against the issuer's published harness
requirements.D01-9.2-downgrade: §9.2: a relying party MUST NOT accept a v0.3-spec receipt against a v0.4-spec gate
requirements.D01-9.2-mapping-tampering: §9.2: receipts MUST bind to a content-addressed mapping; mapping documents MUST be hosted with a stable digest
requirements.D01-10-well-known-jwks: §10: verification issuers using HTTPS SHOULD publish their JWKS at /.well-known/jwks.json per RFC 7517 §4.7 conventions

requirements.EP-4.1-members: review draft §4.1: an evidence_set, when present, MUST be an object with evidence_set_version, retrieved_at, source_count, pinned_count (<= source_count), fully_pinned, evidence_root, sources
requirements.EP-4.1-fully_pinned-stated: review draft §4.1: fully_pinned is stated, not derived; an issuer MUST NOT omit it when some items are unpinned; partial pinning is an honest state
requirements.EP-4.1.1-entry-members: review draft §4.1.1 as amended (rev2 §3): each sources entry carries url, snippet_sha256 (or null), retrieved_at, pinned, and content_kind when pinned
requirements.EP-4.1.1-digest-as-received: review draft §4.1.1 as amended (rev4 Finding 16): snippet_sha256 is computed over the retrieved content exactly as received, the octet sequence as it arrived, with no transcoding, trimming, whitespace collapsing, case folding or Unicode normalization; there is no character-encoding step, the digest is over bytes, not text
requirements.EP-4.1.1-url-bytes: rev2 §3: the url carried in an entry MUST be the URI bytes used for retrieval, without normalization
requirements.EP-4.1.1-possession: rev2 §3 (possession rule): an issuer MUST pin every item for which it received content bytes; every pinned: false entry MUST carry an unpinned_reason from the stated domain; an item outside that domain or without a reason is malformed
requirements.EP-4.1.1-content_kind: rev2 §3 / rev6 Finding 30: content_kind MUST be present and one of the defined values when pinned; on an unpinned entry it MUST be absent or null (equivalent)
requirements.EP-4.1.1-full_resource: rev4 Finding 19 / rev8 Finding 42: a full_resource entry does not carry resource_sha256 (the rule ranges over every entry)
requirements.EP-4.1.1-pinned-boolean: rev8 Finding 40: pinned is REQUIRED on every entry and MUST be exactly true or false; anything else halts
requirements.EP-4.1.2-leaf: review draft §4.1.2 as amended (rev2 Finding 1, rev4 Finding 15a, prefix ao-evidence-leaf-v2): the leaf preimage binds url, snippet_sha256, content_kind and retrieved_at with 0x00 separators
requirements.EP-4.1.2-node: review draft §4.1.2 / rev6 Finding 27: interior node = SHA-256(prefix || 0x00 || left || 0x00 || right) over the raw 32-octet children
requirements.EP-4.1.2-odd-promotion: review draft §4.1.2 / rev6 Finding 28: an odd final entry is promoted unchanged, never duplicated; termination stated
requirements.EP-4.1.2-canonical-order: review draft §4.1.2 as amended (rev4 Finding 15c): leaves sort ascending by the four-term key url, snippet_sha256, content_kind, retrieved_at, bytewise over UTF-8
requirements.EP-4.1.2-domain-separation: review draft §4.1.2: distinct leaf and node prefixes; a leaf hash can never be reinterpreted as a node
requirements.EP-4.1.2-empty-root-null: review draft §4.1.2 / rev8 Finding 43: when pinned_count is zero evidence_root MUST be null; a non-null root with zero pinned entries, or a null root with pinned entries, is malformed
requirements.EP-4.1.2-no-identical-entries: rev5 Finding 24a as amended by rev8 Finding 35: two entries in sources are one retrieval recorded twice when they are identical in url and retrieved_at and, where both are pinned, also identical in snippet_sha256 and content_kind; the rule ranges over every entry, pinned and unpinned alike; malformed, gate decision halt (duplicate_bound_tuple)
requirements.EP-4.1.2-no-identical-entries-mixed-pair: rev8 Finding 35, stated consequence: a pinned entry and an unpinned entry sharing url and retrieved_at are also one retrieval recorded twice and the set halts. rev8 records that no vector in that revision covers this mixed pair
requirements.EP-4.1.2-retrieved_at-form: rev6 Finding 32 / rev8 Finding 37: retrieved_at MUST be RFC 3339 UTC with Z and exactly three fractional digits; the rule ranges over every entry
requirements.EP-4.1-set-retrieved_at-least: rev8 Finding 36: the set-level retrieved_at MUST equal the bytewise-least retrieved_at among all entries
requirements.EP-4.3-a-counts: review draft §4.3 (a) as amended (rev5 24d, rev8 Findings 41, 44): pinned_count, source_count and fully_pinned MUST be consistent with the entries; absent declared counts derive from the entries and MUST NOT halt for want of them
requirements.EP-4.3-a-snippet-required: rev8 Finding 46: step (a) MUST halt on a pinned entry whose snippet_sha256 is absent or null, and MUST NOT let it reach leaf or root construction
requirements.EP-4.3-b-root-recompute: review draft §4.3 (b): a non-null evidence_root is recomputed from sources; a mismatch is malformed and halts
requirements.EP-4.3-c-partial-unknown: §4.3 (c) as restated by rev2 §5: when fully_pinned is false the step resolves unknown, and the receipt MUST NOT be treated as malformed on that account
requirements.EP-4.3-d-content-item-unknown: §4.3 (d) as amended (rev2 §5, rev4 Finding 17, rev8 Finding 45): a content mismatch, or content not held, resolves unknown for that item with a per-item reason (content_differs | content_not_held) and MUST NOT halt
requirements.EP-4.3-e-absent-unknown: §4.3 (e) (review draft (d)): a receipt carrying no evidence_set resolves unknown for the step and MUST NOT fail it
requirements.EP-4.3-f-declared-partial-not-invalid: rev2 §5 step (f): a properly declared partial evidence set is not invalid and the receipt is not malformed; an implementation MUST NOT treat an unknown resolution under (c) as a malformed-receipt condition
requirements.EP-4.3-g-distinct-category: rev2 §5 step (g): a verifier MUST treat an unknown resolution under (c) as a distinct category and MUST NOT present it as a weaker form of a satisfied offline-recompute claim; a verifier that reports, displays, summarises or forwards an outcome MUST carry the distinction
requirements.EP-4.1.2-root-inside-signed-payload: rev2 §5 (Finding 4, Q2): evidence_root MUST be inside the signed payload, without exception
requirements.EP-4.3-resolved-token: rev6 Finding 29: the affirmative step resolution is the token resolved; an implementation MUST emit resolved or unknown and no other value
requirements.EP-4.3-diagnostic-naming: rev6 Finding 31: when more than one condition is violated the implementation halts on the first in section order and names it; a vector injecting more than one condition MUST state which
requirements.EP-4.3-empty-set: rev4 Finding 20: an evidence_set whose sources names no entries is malformed (evidence_set_names_no_sources)
requirements.EP-4.3-condition-identifiers: rev7 Finding 33 / rev8 Finding 38: MALFORMED outcomes are reported with a condition identifier from the registry; superseded identifiers are published as such and fail the build
requirements.EP-5-non-establishment: review draft §5: a pinned evidence set establishes nothing about truth, sufficiency, independence or completeness of retrieval; implementations SHOULD NOT present it as if it did

D01-3.2-conjunction.text: §3.2: multiple verification.* constraints combine with AND; all MUST resolve to act for the action to proceed

D01-3.2-env-ordering.text: §3.2: environment.* constraints MUST short-circuit before verification.* constraints

D01-4.1-jws.text: §4.1: receipts MUST be JWS; a relying party MUST accept compact and JSON (flattened) serializations

D01-4.1-alg.text: §4.1: a conforming implementation MUST accept both EdDSA and ES256

D01-4.1-kid.text: §4.1: kid MUST resolve to a key in the issuer's published JWKS

D01-4.2-v_verdict.text: §4.2: v_verdict REQUIRED, one of supported | refuted | unverifiable | unknown

D01-4.2-v_adversarial_result.text: §4.2: v_adversarial_result REQUIRED, one of resilient | vulnerable | not_checked

D01-4.2-v_recommendation.text: §4.2: v_recommendation REQUIRED, derived deterministically from the canonical input under the named mapping

D01-4.2-v_gate.text: §4.2: v_gate REQUIRED, act | halt, derived from v_recommendation under the named mapping

D01-4.2-v_gate_mapping.text: §4.2: v_gate_mapping REQUIRED; mapping documents are immutable after publication

D01-4.2-v_gate_mapping_hash.text: §4.2: v_gate_mapping_hash REQUIRED; absence is a malformed-receipt condition and MUST halt

D01-4.2-jwt-claims.text: §4.2: iss, iat, exp REQUIRED; sub RECOMMENDED; nbf OPTIONAL

D01-4.3-sequence.text: §4.3: a relying party MUST execute the eight-step sequence and treat any failure as malformed with gate decision halt

D01-4.3-1-signature.text: §4.3 step 1: verify the JWS signature against the issuer's published JWKS

D01-4.3-2-mapping-digest.text: §4.3 step 2: fetch the named mapping document; its SHA-256 MUST match v_gate_mapping_hash; receipts without the hash are malformed

D01-4.3-3-recompute-recommendation.text: §4.3 step 3: recompute candidate_recommendation from (v_verdict, v_confidence, v_adversarial_result) using the mapping's rules and threshold

D01-4.3-7-time.text: §4.3 step 7: verify exp/nbf against current time subject to clock tolerance

D01-4.3-8-mismatch-halts.text: §4.3 step 8: any mismatch -> malformed; gate decision = halt

D01-4.4-v_claim.text: §4.4: the verified claim MUST be bound via v_claim (text, or hash REQUIRED when text is omitted)

D01-4.5-mapping-hash-present.text: §4.5: v_gate_mapping_hash MUST be present in all conforming receipts

D01-4.6-old-mapping-verifiable.text: §4.6: a receipt issued under an older mapping MUST remain verifiable as correct under that mapping

D01-4.6-mapping-immutable.text: §4.6: publishers MUST treat published mappings as immutable; new rules ship under new identifiers

D01-5.1-table-shape.text: §5.1: the binary act/halt shape derived from the canonical recommendation MUST be preserved

D01-5.1-row-1.text: §5.1 Table 2 row 1: supported, >= threshold, resilient -> confident_supported -> act

D01-5.1-row-2.text: §5.1 Table 2 row 2: supported, >= threshold, not_checked -> un_probed_not_cleared -> halt

D01-5.1-row-3.text: §5.1 Table 2 row 3: supported, any, vulnerable -> vulnerable_supported -> halt

D01-5.1-row-4.text: §5.1 Table 2 row 4: supported, < threshold, resilient or not_checked -> weak_supported -> halt

D01-5.1-row-6.text: §5.1 Table 2 row 6: unverifiable or unknown -> unverifiable -> halt

D01-5.1-row-7.text: §5.1 Table 2 row 7: error condition -> error -> halt

D01-5.2-threshold-from-mapping.text: §5.2: the threshold is recovered from the named mapping; two receipts under one mapping ID MUST gate against the same threshold

D01-5.2-uncertainty-halts.text: §5.2: un-probed adversarial state is not equivalent to resilient; uncertainty MUST halt (un_probed_not_cleared)

D01-5.2-no-foreign-threshold.text: §5.2: relying parties MUST NOT treat a receipt as conformant under a mapping with a different threshold than that mapping states

D01-5.3-fail-closed.text: §5.3: missing, malformed, expired, signature-invalid or unresolvable-mapping receipts MUST be treated as halt; implementations MUST NOT default to act

D01-6.2-stale-signature.text: §6.2: a stale signature makes the receipt invalid; relying party MUST treat as halt

D01-6.2-stale-calibration.text: §6.2: stale calibration SHOULD be re-evaluated; issuers SHOULD publish recalibration cadence

D01-6.2-stale-evidence.text: §6.2: stale evidence SHOULD be re-evaluated and MUST NOT be honored as a gate signal for new actions

D01-7.1-publish-anchors.text: §7.1: verifier issuers MUST publish calibration anchors (the listed items)

D01-7.1-harness.text: §7.1: verifier issuers SHOULD publish a reference reproduction harness under a permissive license

D01-7.2-cadence.text: §7.2: issuers SHOULD publish a recalibration cadence; v_calibration.valid_until SHOULD reflect it

D01-7.2-surface-stale.text: §7.2: relying parties consuming receipts with stale calibration SHOULD log and surface the staleness rather than silently accept

D01-9.1-ordering-holds.text: §9.1: the §3.2 ordering MUST hold when composed with environment.*

D01-9.2-key-rotation.text: §9.2: issuers MUST rotate JWKS keys on a published cadence; RPs MUST honor key revocation lists where published

D01-9.2-replay.text: §9.2: RPs MUST verify iat and exp against current time

D01-9.2-sample-harness.text: §9.2 (confidence inflation): RPs SHOULD periodically sample receipts against the issuer's published harness

D01-9.2-downgrade.text: §9.2: a relying party MUST NOT accept a v0.3-spec receipt against a v0.4-spec gate

D01-9.2-mapping-tampering.text: §9.2: receipts MUST bind to a content-addressed mapping; mapping documents MUST be hosted with a stable digest

D01-10-well-known-jwks.text: §10: verification issuers using HTTPS SHOULD publish their JWKS at /.well-known/jwks.json per RFC 7517 §4.7 conventions

D01.note: rule2 vectors count here but are labelled NOT NORMATIVE in their manifest; a reader wanting the normative-only view removes them

RMT-action-ref.text: action_ref is computed per draft-giskard-aeoess-action-ref over agent_id, action_type, scope, timestamp (RFC 3339 UTC, exactly 3 fractional digits)

RMT-trail-sibling.text: a returned mycelium_trail_id can be carried at the envelope level as a sibling pointer to v_gate (the composed-envelope spec it defers to is described as forthcoming)

MAP-rule-4.text: rule 4: supported, < threshold, resilient or not_checked -> weak_supported

MAP-gate_map.text: gate_map: only confident_supported -> act; every other recommendation -> halt

MAP-threshold.text: threshold: v_confidence >= 0.7; the threshold lives in the mapping, not in receipts

MAP.note: exercised only by the NOT NORMATIVE rule2 set

EP-4.1-members.text: review draft §4.1: an evidence_set, when present, MUST be an object with evidence_set_version, retrieved_at, source_count, pinned_count (<= source_count), fully_pinned, evidence_root, sources

EP-4.1-fully_pinned-stated.text: review draft §4.1: fully_pinned is stated, not derived; an issuer MUST NOT omit it when some items are unpinned; partial pinning is an honest state

EP-4.1.1-entry-members.text: review draft §4.1.1 as amended (rev2 §3): each sources entry carries url, snippet_sha256 (or null), retrieved_at, pinned, and content_kind when pinned

EP-4.1.1-digest-as-received.text: review draft §4.1.1 as amended (rev4 Finding 16): snippet_sha256 is computed over the retrieved content exactly as received, the octet sequence as it arrived, with no transcoding, trimming, whitespace collapsing, case folding or Unicode normalization; there is no character-encoding step, the digest is over bytes, not text

EP-4.1.1-url-bytes.text: rev2 §3: the url carried in an entry MUST be the URI bytes used for retrieval, without normalization

EP-4.1.1-possession.text: rev2 §3 (possession rule): an issuer MUST pin every item for which it received content bytes; every pinned: false entry MUST carry an unpinned_reason from the stated domain; an item outside that domain or without a reason is malformed

EP-4.1.1-content_kind.text: rev2 §3 / rev6 Finding 30: content_kind MUST be present and one of the defined values when pinned; on an unpinned entry it MUST be absent or null (equivalent)

EP-4.1.1-full_resource.text: rev4 Finding 19 / rev8 Finding 42: a full_resource entry does not carry resource_sha256 (the rule ranges over every entry)

EP-4.1.1-pinned-boolean.text: rev8 Finding 40: pinned is REQUIRED on every entry and MUST be exactly true or false; anything else halts

EP-4.1.2-leaf.text: review draft §4.1.2 as amended (rev2 Finding 1, rev4 Finding 15a, prefix ao-evidence-leaf-v2): the leaf preimage binds url, snippet_sha256, content_kind and retrieved_at with 0x00 separators

EP-4.1.2-node.text: review draft §4.1.2 / rev6 Finding 27: interior node = SHA-256(prefix || 0x00 || left || 0x00 || right) over the raw 32-octet children

EP-4.1.2-odd-promotion.text: review draft §4.1.2 / rev6 Finding 28: an odd final entry is promoted unchanged, never duplicated; termination stated

EP-4.1.2-canonical-order.text: review draft §4.1.2 as amended (rev4 Finding 15c): leaves sort ascending by the four-term key url, snippet_sha256, content_kind, retrieved_at, bytewise over UTF-8

EP-4.1.2-domain-separation.text: review draft §4.1.2: distinct leaf and node prefixes; a leaf hash can never be reinterpreted as a node

EP-4.1.2-empty-root-null.text: review draft §4.1.2 / rev8 Finding 43: when pinned_count is zero evidence_root MUST be null; a non-null root with zero pinned entries, or a null root with pinned entries, is malformed

EP-4.1.2-no-identical-entries.text: rev5 Finding 24a as amended by rev8 Finding 35: two entries in sources are one retrieval recorded twice when they are identical in url and retrieved_at and, where both are pinned, also identical in snippet_sha256 and content_kind; the rule ranges over every entry, pinned and unpinned alike; malformed, gate decision halt (duplicate_bound_tuple)

EP-4.1.2-no-identical-entries-mixed-pair.text: rev8 Finding 35, stated consequence: a pinned entry and an unpinned entry sharing url and retrieved_at are also one retrieval recorded twice and the set halts. rev8 records that no vector in that revision covers this mixed pair

EP-4.1.2-retrieved_at-form.text: rev6 Finding 32 / rev8 Finding 37: retrieved_at MUST be RFC 3339 UTC with Z and exactly three fractional digits; the rule ranges over every entry

EP-4.1-set-retrieved_at-least.text: rev8 Finding 36: the set-level retrieved_at MUST equal the bytewise-least retrieved_at among all entries

EP-4.3-a-counts.text: review draft §4.3 (a) as amended (rev5 24d, rev8 Findings 41, 44): pinned_count, source_count and fully_pinned MUST be consistent with the entries; absent declared counts derive from the entries and MUST NOT halt for want of them

EP-4.3-a-snippet-required.text: rev8 Finding 46: step (a) MUST halt on a pinned entry whose snippet_sha256 is absent or null, and MUST NOT let it reach leaf or root construction

EP-4.3-b-root-recompute.text: review draft §4.3 (b): a non-null evidence_root is recomputed from sources; a mismatch is malformed and halts

EP-4.3-c-partial-unknown.text: §4.3 (c) as restated by rev2 §5: when fully_pinned is false the step resolves unknown, and the receipt MUST NOT be treated as malformed on that account

EP-4.3-d-content-item-unknown.text: §4.3 (d) as amended (rev2 §5, rev4 Finding 17, rev8 Finding 45): a content mismatch, or content not held, resolves unknown for that item with a per-item reason (content_differs | content_not_held) and MUST NOT halt

EP-4.3-e-absent-unknown.text: §4.3 (e) (review draft (d)): a receipt carrying no evidence_set resolves unknown for the step and MUST NOT fail it

EP-4.3-f-declared-partial-not-invalid.text: rev2 §5 step (f): a properly declared partial evidence set is not invalid and the receipt is not malformed; an implementation MUST NOT treat an unknown resolution under (c) as a malformed-receipt condition

EP-4.3-g-distinct-category.text: rev2 §5 step (g): a verifier MUST treat an unknown resolution under (c) as a distinct category and MUST NOT present it as a weaker form of a satisfied offline-recompute claim; a verifier that reports, displays, summarises or forwards an outcome MUST carry the distinction

EP-4.1.2-root-inside-signed-payload.text: rev2 §5 (Finding 4, Q2): evidence_root MUST be inside the signed payload, without exception

EP-4.3-resolved-token.text: rev6 Finding 29: the affirmative step resolution is the token resolved; an implementation MUST emit resolved or unknown and no other value

EP-4.3-diagnostic-naming.text: rev6 Finding 31: when more than one condition is violated the implementation halts on the first in section order and names it; a vector injecting more than one condition MUST state which

EP-4.3-empty-set.text: rev4 Finding 20: an evidence_set whose sources names no entries is malformed (evidence_set_names_no_sources)

EP-4.3-condition-identifiers.text: rev7 Finding 33 / rev8 Finding 38: MALFORMED outcomes are reported with a condition identifier from the registry; superseded identifiers are published as such and fail the build

EP-5-non-establishment.text: review draft §5: a pinned evidence set establishes nothing about truth, sufficiency, independence or completeness of retrieval; implementations SHOULD NOT present it as if it did
